# Operability and observability — 1.1.0

## Apply when

Use for every production or business-critical capability.

## Required context

Service owner, support model, critical journeys, SLOs, deployment model, environments, telemetry, incident process, maintenance windows, and operational dependencies.

## Clarify

Ask who responds to incidents, which user outcomes define health, what deployment and rollback targets apply, and which operational tasks remain manual.

## Deterministic checks

- Flag services without ownership, SLOs, actionable alerts, dashboards, runbooks, or escalation paths.
- Check logs, metrics, traces, correlation, audit events, synthetic checks, dependency health, and capacity signals.
- Check safe deployment, rollback, configuration change, feature control, maintenance, and break-glass procedures.
- Identify alert noise, unbounded telemetry cost, inaccessible diagnostics, and manual recovery dependencies.
- Do not claim operational readiness without an observed exercise or production evidence.

## Research

Research current telemetry capabilities, retention limits, or service integrations only when they affect feasibility. Prefer official product documentation.

## Output

Produce an ownership and SLO summary, observability coverage, operational readiness gaps, exercise plan, and standard findings.
